### `machines.*.files[].mode`

The file's permissions, in octal (`0600`, `0755`; default `0644`), quoted or not: the digits are kept as written. Linux machines only.

- **Type:** string or number or boolean
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { files: [{ path: /etc/app.ini, content: x, mode: '0600' }] } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`
- **Refused by:** `external`: machine `a` has `files`: Isoloom doesn't write on an existing host, so place them with a `provision:` playbook
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.disks`

Data disks beside the machine's own, by name (kebab-case, at most 12 characters: the filesystem's label): `{ size_gb: 50, fs: xfs, mount: /data }`. A VM gets an empty disk of that size, formatted and mounted at boot; a container gets a volume at the mount. The disks go with the machine.

- **Type:** map of name to mapping

### `machines.*.disks.*.size_gb`

Its size in GB (1 to 16384).

- **Type:** integer
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { disks: { data: { size_gb: 50, mount: /data } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid` (not yet: QEMU, Parallels and UTM attach none (refused there))
- **Refused by:** `external`: machine `a` has data disks (`disks`), which this target can't attach
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.disks.*.fs`

Its filesystem: `ext4` (the default on Linux), `xfs`, `ntfs` (the default on Windows), or `raw` for a block device left unformatted.

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `ext4`: Linux's usual filesystem.
  - `xfs`: XFS, for large files.
  - `ntfs`: Windows' filesystem.
  - `raw`: No filesystem: a block device the machine formats or uses itself.
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { disks: { data: { size_gb: 50, fs: xfs, mount: /data } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Partly rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize` (not yet: the filesystem's type: the storage class picks it)
- **Refused by:** `external`: machine `a` has data disks (`disks`), which this target can't attach
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.disks.*.mount`

Where it is mounted: an absolute path on Linux and in containers, a drive letter (`E:`) on Windows. Required unless the disk is `raw`.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { disks: { data: { size_gb: 50, mount: /data } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`
- **Refused by:** `external`: machine `a` has data disks (`disks`), which this target can't attach
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.access`

The machine the user lands on. It may have no implementation: the runner supplies it.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `machines: { b: { access: true } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `cloud-vm` (linode), `cloud-vm` (oci), `cloud-docker`, `external`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid` (not yet: checks don't run from it)
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm takes one machine on one network: a droplet joins one VPC, at a private address DigitalOcean picks, so other machines couldn't reach it at its spec address
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

## `machines.*.docker`

### `machines.*.docker`

How a container produces this machine: an image or a build, and what only a container has (init jobs, appliances). A machine with `docker:` can run on the container targets.

- **Type:** mapping

### `machines.*.docker.image`

A published image (exactly one of `image` and `build`).

- **Type:** string
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.build`

A folder of the project, built into the machine's image as its build context (exactly one of `image` and `build`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { image: null, build: app } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Partly rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize` (not yet: the build itself: the image is built and pushed by hand)
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.dockerfile`

The Dockerfile, a file anywhere in the project (default: `Dockerfile` in `build`): an image of your own around a vendored project's source, without moving that source.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { image: null, build: app, dockerfile: app.Dockerfile } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Partly rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize` (not yet: the build itself)
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.target`

The stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile to build (`FROM ... AS <target>`), when not its last: the lab's image beside the release one, from one Dockerfile.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { image: null, build: app, target: lab } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Partly rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize` (not yet: the build itself)
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.args`

Build arguments (`ARG`s of the Dockerfile), fixed values.

- **Type:** map of name to string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { image: null, build: app, args: { MODE: lab } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Partly rendered by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize` (not yet: the build itself)
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.init`

One-shot jobs (scripts or folders in the project) run before the machine counts as ready.

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { init: [init.sh] } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.idle`

The image runs no service of its own (a stock Linux image whose command is a shell that exits at once): keep the container running idle, as a machine to work from.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { idle: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Not used by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.appliance`

The image is a network appliance Isoloom knows how to wire (a router or switch OS in a container): its management port, interface order and startup configuration are set the way the image expects, its addresses go into that configuration. Docker only.

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `cisco-iol`: Cisco IOL (IOS on Linux, from Cisco Modeling Labs) as vrnetlab packages it (`vrnetlab/cisco_iol:<version>`): a router.
  - `cisco-iol-l2`: Cisco IOL-L2 (`vrnetlab/cisco_iol:L2-<version>`): a switch.
  - `cisco-vios`: Cisco IOSv in QEMU (`vrnetlab/cisco_vios:<version>`, needs /dev/kvm): a router.
  - `cisco-vios-l2`: Cisco IOSvL2 in QEMU (`vrnetlab/cisco_viosl2:<version>`, needs /dev/kvm): a switch. `cisco-viosl2`, as the image is named, is read too.
  - `cisco-csr1000v`: Cisco CSR1000v (IOS XE) in QEMU (`vrnetlab/cisco_csr1000v:<version>`, needs /dev/kvm).
  - `cisco-c8000v`: Cisco Catalyst 8000v (IOS XE) in QEMU (`vrnetlab/cisco_c8000v:<version>`, needs /dev/kvm).
  - `cisco-dynamips`: A classic Cisco 7200 router emulated by Dynamips, booting the IOS `.bin` in `firmware`.
- **Example:** `machines: { r: { docker: { image: vrnetlab/cisco_iol, appliance: cisco-iol } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`: machine `r` is a network appliance (`docker.appliance`), which runs on the Docker targets
- **Not used by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.config`

An appliance's own configuration (a file in the project), added to the one Isoloom generates (hostname, credentials, interfaces and their addresses).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { r: { docker: { image: vrnetlab/cisco_iol, appliance: cisco-iol, config: r1.cfg } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`: machine `r` is a network appliance (`docker.appliance`), which runs on the Docker targets
- **Not used by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.firmware`

The firmware an emulator boots (a file in the project): the IOS `.bin` of a Dynamips router. Isoloom builds the emulator's container itself, so no `image` then.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { r: { docker: { appliance: cisco-dynamips, firmware: c7200.bin } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`: machine `r` is a network appliance (`docker.appliance`), which runs on the Docker targets
- **Not used by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.docker.lxc`

On Proxmox, a machine with no `vm:` may run as an LXC container from its `image` (an OCI image, Proxmox VE 9.1 or later) instead of ruling the `proxmox` target out. Opt-in: an LXC container is no Docker container (no Docker runtime, no healthcheck, no named volumes), so the author says the image runs as one. Ignored by every other target.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { docker: { lxc: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

## `machines.*.vm`

### `machines.*.vm`

How a VM produces this machine (services installed natively, no Docker inside).

- **Type:** mapping

### `machines.*.vm.os`

The OS, one of the names Isoloom knows; each target maps it to an image. May come from `common:` or a group (`vm: {}` in the machine).

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:** `debian-11`, `debian-12`, `debian-13`, `ubuntu-14.04`, `ubuntu-16.04`, `ubuntu-18.04`, `ubuntu-20.04`, `ubuntu-22.04`, `ubuntu-24.04`, `rocky-9`, `almalinux-9`, `centos-7`, `fedora-42`, `kali`, `windows-10`, `windows-11`, `windows-server-2008r2`, `windows-server-2012r2`, `windows-server-2016`, `windows-server-2019`, `windows-server-2022`, `windows-server-2025`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Partly rendered by:** `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud) (not yet: Kali)
- **Partly rendered by:** `external` (not yet: Windows hosts skip the machine's own steps)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.vm.provision`

Steps run inside the VM, in order: `.sh` on Linux (and Ansible playbooks, `.yml`), `.ps1` on Windows. On Linux, the step `reboot` restarts the machine and goes on with the next step once it is back (a new kernel, a changed boot configuration).

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Partly rendered by:** `external` (not yet: Windows hosts)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`

### `machines.*.vm.image`

The image to use instead of the built-in one for `os`, per target.

- **Type:** mapping

### `machines.*.vm.image.vagrant`

A Vagrant box name (e.g. `StefanScherer/windows_2019`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { vagrant: debian/bookworm64 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.vagrant_version`

The box version to pin.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { vagrant: debian/bookworm64, vagrant_version: 12.20240503.1 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.qemu`

The box Vagrant's QEMU provider boots instead (libvirt format), when `vagrant` has none (e.g. `peru/windows-server-2019-standard-x64-eval`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { qemu: generic/debian12 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.hyperv`

The box Vagrant's Hyper-V provider boots instead, when `vagrant` has no Hyper-V build (its latest version that has one).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { hyperv: generic/debian12 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.winrm`

How this Windows box answers WinRM, when it isn't the usual plain-HTTP box.

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `plaintext`: HTTP on 5985, basic auth (the default for the common Windows boxes).
  - `ssl`: HTTPS on 5986, NTLM (certificate not verified).
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { os: windows-server-2022, provision: [setup.ps1], image: { winrm: plaintext } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.winssh`

This Windows box answers OpenSSH (Windows' own `sshd`, PowerShell as its shell) instead of WinRM: Vagrant connects with `config.winssh` and the playbooks over SSH, as the box's `vagrant` account. Not with `winrm`.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { os: windows-server-2022, provision: [setup.ps1], image: { winssh: true } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.box_url`

Where Vagrant downloads the `vagrant` box from, when it isn't on Vagrant Cloud: a URL, or a `.box` file in the project (list its folder in `.isoloomignore`, or the project copied into every VM carries it).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { vagrant: debian/bookworm64, box_url: 'https://boxes.example/debian.box' } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.box_server_url`

The box server Vagrant looks the `vagrant` box up on, instead of Vagrant Cloud (a private registry).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { vagrant: debian/bookworm64, box_server_url: 'https://boxes.example' } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.proxmox`

The Proxmox image: a cloud image's URL (the server downloads it), or the id of a template VM on the node (cloned).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { proxmox: '9000' } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`, `esxi`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.aws`

The AWS image: an AMI id (`ami-0123...`) in the module's region.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { aws: ami-0123456789abcdef0 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.azure`

The Azure image: a managed image's or gallery image version's resource id.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { azure: /subscriptions/s/resourceGroups/g/providers/Microsoft.Compute/images/i } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.gcp`

The Google Cloud image: `projects/<project>/global/images/<image>` (or `.../family/<f>`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { gcp: projects/p/global/images/i } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.digitalocean`

The DigitalOcean image: a slug or a custom image's id.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { digitalocean: '123456' } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.linode`

The Linode image: `linode/<distribution>` or `private/<id>`.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { linode: private/123 } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.image.oci`

The Oracle Cloud image: its OCID (`ocid1.image...`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { image: { oci: ocid1.image.oc1..example } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.tpm`

A virtual TPM 2.0 (BitLocker, Windows Hello, measured boot). Unset, a Windows 11 machine gets one wherever the target can give one, and runs without where it can't (its built-in images install without one). `true` requires one: a target that gives none refuses the environment. `false` gives none.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { tpm: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`
- **Partly rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `cloud-vm` (oci) (not yet: Windows on AWS (Amazon's NitroTPM Windows images))
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` asks for a virtual TPM (`vm.tpm: true`), which this target doesn't give (Vagrant on VirtualBox, libvirt or Hyper-V, Proxmox and the big clouds do)
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): machine `a` asks for a virtual TPM (`vm.tpm: true`): DigitalOcean gives none
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): machine `a` asks for a virtual TPM (`vm.tpm: true`): Linode gives none
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot`

How it boots, when not the way its image does: its own kernel, firmware, boot order or network boot.

- **Type:** mapping

### `machines.*.vm.boot.kernel`

A kernel to boot directly, instead of the image's boot loader.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { kernel: /boot/vmlinuz } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `proxmox`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: Proxmox boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware`, `order` and `firmware_format` apply); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.initrd`

The initial RAM disk booted with `kernel`.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { kernel: /boot/vmlinuz, initrd: /boot/initrd.img } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `proxmox`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: Proxmox boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware`, `order` and `firmware_format` apply); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.cmdline`

The command line passed to `kernel` (`console=ttyS0 root=/dev/vda1`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { kernel: /boot/vmlinuz, cmdline: console=ttyS0 } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `proxmox`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: Proxmox boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware`, `order` and `firmware_format` apply); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.dtb`

A device tree blob for `kernel` (ARM boards).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { kernel: /boot/vmlinuz, dtb: /boot/board.dtb } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it

- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.kernel`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.firmware`

The firmware the VM boots through: `bios`, or `uefi` (on libvirt, with its file in `loader`; Proxmox and QEMU bring their own).

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `bios`: A legacy BIOS (SeaBIOS).
  - `uefi`: UEFI (OVMF).
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { firmware: uefi } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`, `esxi`

- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.loader`

A UEFI firmware file the VM boots through (OVMF's `OVMF_CODE.fd`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { loader: /usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE.fd } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `proxmox`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.loader`: Proxmox boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware`, `order` and `firmware_format` apply); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.loader`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.nvram`

The file that keeps the firmware's variables between boots (with `loader`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { loader: /usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE.fd, nvram: /var/lib/a_VARS.fd } } } }`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: refused on the providers that boot the box as it is (VirtualBox, VMware, Parallels, UTM, Hyper-V, ESXi, QEMU))
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `proxmox`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.loader`: Proxmox boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware`, `order` and `firmware_format` apply); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.loader`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.firmware_format`

The format of the UEFI firmware files the hypervisor loads: `raw` (QEMU's own, as Homebrew ships them) or `qcow2` (some distributions'). Vagrant's QEMU provider needs it to load them; libvirt reads the format from the file itself.

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `raw`: A raw image (QEMU's `edk2-*-code.fd`).
  - `qcow2`: A qcow2 image.
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { firmware: uefi, firmware_format: raw } } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Partly rendered by:** `vagrant` (not yet: libvirt reads the format from the file; the other providers refuse it)
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Refused by:** `esxi`: machine `a` sets `vm.boot.firmware_format`: ESXi boots the VM's disk through its own firmware (`firmware` applies, as `boot_firmware`); Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.order`

The devices to boot from, in order (`[network, hd]` tries a network boot first).

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { vm: { boot: { order: [hd, network] } } } }`

- **Refused by:** `hybrid`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud): machine `a` boots its own way (`vm.boot`): this target boots a VM from its image's own kernel and firmware; Vagrant's libvirt provider boots it

- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.network`

A network boot served on the machine's first network: its TFTP folder and the file DHCP hands out. `order` must list `network`.

- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `machines.*.vm.boot.network.file`

The boot file DHCP hands out (`pxelinux.0`), from the TFTP folder.

- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

## `machines.*.external`

### `machines.*.external`

Where this machine already exists (the `external` target): Isoloom creates nothing and reaches it over SSH to provision, check and connect.

- **Type:** mapping

### `machines.*.external.address`

An address or hostname reachable from where Isoloom runs.

- **Type:** string
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the `external` target's SSH endpoint (inventory, checks, connect)
- **Rendered by:** `external`

### `machines.*.external.user`

The SSH user (default `root`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { external: { user: admin } } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the `external` target's SSH user
- **Rendered by:** `external`

### `machines.*.external.port`

The SSH port (default 22).

- **Type:** integer
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { external: { port: 2222 } } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the `external` target's SSH port
- **Rendered by:** `external`

### `machines.*.external.key`

A private key file (default: the SSH agent and config).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `machines: { a: { external: { key: ~/.ssh/lab } } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the `external` target's SSH key
- **Rendered by:** `external`

## `cloud`

### `cloud`

An environment of cloud services rather than machines (IAM users and roles, functions, buckets, queues...): a Terraform module in the project, applied into the user's own cloud account. A spec has either `cloud:` or machines.

- **Type:** mapping

### `cloud.provider`

The cloud the module deploys into (its credentials come from the environment, as Terraform expects).

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `aws`: Amazon Web Services.
  - `azure`: Microsoft Azure.
  - `gcp`: Google Cloud.
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the cloud of a cloud-services environment (the cloud-services target, not these outputs)
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.terraform`

A Terraform root module in the project (a folder holding `.tf` files), used as is.

- **Type:** string
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the Terraform module the cloud-services target applies
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.vars`

The module's variables: any value (a string, number, boolean, list or map). A string holding `{{ inputs.NAME }}`, at any depth (`["{{ inputs.PLAYER_IP }}/32"]`), takes the launch-time input `NAME` (declared in `inputs`), e.g. the user's IP for an allow-list: required at `run`, kept for `down`.

- **Type:** mapping
- **Example:** `cloud: { vars: { region: us-east-1 } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** the module's variables (terraform.tfvars.json)
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.outputs`

What the environment exposes, by name: a module output each. Checks and the message use them as `{{ cloud.outputs.<name> }}`.

- **Type:** map of name to string
- **Example:** `cloud: { outputs: { site: url } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** what checks and the message read once deployed
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.hourly_usd`

About what the environment costs per hour while it exists, in US dollars: the author's estimate, for whoever runs it. `isoloom run` says it before applying, and the resolved snapshot carries it (`cloud.hourly_usd`) for anything that shows costs or keeps to a budget. Isoloom doesn't bill or stop anything by it.

- **Type:** number
- **Example:** `cloud: { hourly_usd: 0.01 }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** an estimate: `isoloom run` says it, the snapshot carries it
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.before`

Steps run on this machine before Terraform applies the module (a key pair the module reads, a build): scripts in the project, run in order from the module's copy, with the spec's inputs and `env` in their environment. They run at every `run`: make them idempotent.

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Example:** `cloud: { before: [setup.sh] }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** host steps before the apply (up.sh)
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.env`

Environment variables for Terraform and the `before` steps (`AWS_REGION: us-east-1`). Not for credentials: those come from the user's own environment.

- **Type:** map of name to string
- **Example:** `cloud: { env: { AWS_REGION: us-east-1 } }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** Terraform's environment (the cloud-services scripts)
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.apply_retries`

How many times to apply again when an apply fails (a module that only converges on a second apply), 0 to 5. 0 by default.

- **Type:** integer
- **Example:** `cloud: { apply_retries: 2 }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** applies again after a failed apply (up.sh)
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

### `cloud.requires`

What the module needs on this machine besides Terraform: a command name (`jq`, `gsed`) that must be on the PATH, or a shell command that must succeed (`python3 -c 'import boto3'`). `isoloom doctor` and `isoloom run` check them.

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Example:** `cloud: { requires: [jq] }`
- **Read by Isoloom itself:** host tools `doctor` and `run` check
- **Rendered by:** `cloud-services`

## `volumes`

### `volumes`

Volumes shared between machines: a machine volume with one of these names is this volume, wherever it mounts it. One declared here can also outlive `isoloom down` (`persistent: true`) or be one that exists already (`external: <name>`).

- **Type:** map of name to mapping

### `volumes.*.owner`

The machine that holds the data (serves it over NFS on the VM targets). Default: the first machine that mounts it.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { owner: a } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`
- **Partly rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `cloud-vm` (linode), `cloud-vm` (oci) (not yet: Windows machines)
- **Refused by:** `hybrid`: volume `data` is shared by containers and VMs: one storage can't be both a Docker volume and an NFS export, for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm takes one machine on one network: a droplet joins one VPC, at a private address DigitalOcean picks, so other machines couldn't reach it at its spec address
- **Planned for:** `external`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `volumes.*.persistent`

Keep its data when the environment is torn down: `isoloom down` leaves it, and the next `run` finds it again; `isoloom down --volumes` removes it. Docker and Kubernetes; a VM's storage goes with the VM.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { persistent: true } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`
- **Refused by:** `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `external`: volume `data` is persistent: it outlives `down` on Docker and Kubernetes, while this target's storage goes with its machines
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `volumes.*.external`

An existing volume, by its name on the platform (a Docker volume, a Kubernetes claim in the environment's namespace): Isoloom mounts it and never creates or removes it.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { external: lab-data } }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`
- **Refused by:** `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `external`: volume `data` is an existing one (`external`): Docker and Kubernetes mount one by name, this target has none to mount
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `volumes.*.virtiofs`

On Proxmox, the volume as a folder of the server, shared into each VM that mounts it (virtiofs) instead of over NFS from its owner: `virtiofs: {}` takes the defaults. Every other target ignores it.

- **Type:** mapping

### `volumes.*.virtiofs.mapping`

An existing directory mapping of the cluster, by its id (Datacenter, Resource Mappings, Directory mappings). By default Isoloom creates one, `iso<slot>-<volume>`, for the folder `<virtiofs_root>/<environment>/<volume>` on the node.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { virtiofs: { mapping: lab-data, cache: never, direct_io: true, xattr: true, acl: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `volumes.*.virtiofs.cache`

How the guests cache the folder: `auto` (the default: metadata kept a short while, so another VM's changes show within a second), `always`, `metadata` or `never` (every access goes to the server: slowest, always current).

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `auto`: Metadata and lookups kept a short while, or until they change: Proxmox's default.
  - `always`: Everything kept: fastest, but another VM's changes may not show.
  - `metadata`: Metadata kept, data read each time.
  - `never`: Nothing kept: every access goes to the server.
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { virtiofs: { mapping: lab-data, cache: never, direct_io: true, xattr: true, acl: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `volumes.*.virtiofs.direct_io`

Reads and writes that bypass the guest's page cache when a program asks for it (`O_DIRECT`), for databases that manage their own cache. Off by default.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { virtiofs: { mapping: lab-data, cache: never, direct_io: true, xattr: true, acl: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `volumes.*.virtiofs.xattr`

Pass extended attributes through (SELinux labels, file capabilities). Off by default.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { virtiofs: { mapping: lab-data, cache: never, direct_io: true, xattr: true, acl: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `volumes.*.virtiofs.acl`

Pass POSIX ACLs through (`setfacl`), which implies `xattr`. Off by default.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `volumes: { data: { virtiofs: { mapping: lab-data, cache: never, direct_io: true, xattr: true, acl: true } } }`
- **Rendered by:** `proxmox`
- **Not used by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

## `constraints`

### `constraints`

What the place it runs in imposes: an HTTP proxy, registry and package mirrors, time servers. Usually set by a profile, one customer's network at a time.

- **Type:** mapping

### `constraints.proxy`

The HTTP proxy outbound traffic goes through: set for the machines' containers (and their builds) and on every Linux VM (shell, apt, dnf, Docker), never for Isoloom's own checks.

- **Type:** mapping

### `constraints.proxy.http`

The proxy for `http://` URLs, e.g. `http://proxy.corp:3128`.

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.proxy.https`

The proxy for `https://` URLs (default: `http`'s).

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.proxy.no_proxy`

Names, domains (`.corp`) and blocks reached directly. The environment's own machine names and network blocks, and localhost, are always added.

- **Type:** list of strings

### `constraints.registries`

Registry mirrors, by the registry they stand for: `docker.io: registry.corp/dockerhub` pulls `redis:7` as `registry.corp/dockerhub/library/redis:7`. Every image of the environment is rewritten, Isoloom's own included; images built from the project aren't pulled, so they stay as they are (their `FROM` lines are the Dockerfile's business).

- **Type:** map of name to string

### `constraints.mirrors`

Package mirrors the machines install from instead of the public archives: apt's for Debian and Ubuntu VMs, and a Python package index.

- **Type:** mapping

### `constraints.mirrors.debian`

Replaces `deb.debian.org/debian` in the Debian VMs' apt sources (`debian-security`, a separate archive, is left as it is).

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.mirrors.ubuntu`

Replaces `archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu` (and its country and security hosts) in the Ubuntu VMs' apt sources.

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.mirrors.pypi`

A Python package index: `PIP_INDEX_URL` for the machines, `/etc/pip.conf` on the VMs.

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.mirrors.npm`

An npm registry: `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` for the machines, `/etc/npmrc` on the VMs.

- **Type:** string

### `constraints.ntp`

The time servers (names or addresses) the Linux VMs synchronise their clocks with, where the place forbids the public pools.

- **Type:** list of strings

## `provision`

### `provision`

Provisioning across machines, once every machine is up: Ansible playbooks run from a controller on the environment's networks, with an inventory Isoloom writes.

- **Type:** list of mappings

### `provision[].ansible`

An Ansible playbook in the project, run against the whole environment.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `external`
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `provision[].inventory`

More inventory files in the project (groups, variables), next to the one Isoloom writes (every machine's address and connection, in the `linux` or `windows` group).

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml, inventory: [extra.ini] }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `external`
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `provision[].groups`

Inventory groups: a name -> the machines in it.

- **Type:** map of name to list of strings
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml, groups: { web: [a] } }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `external`
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `provision[].vars`

Extra variables for the playbook, of any YAML type (strings, numbers, booleans, lists, maps): passed as JSON (`-e`), which keeps their types.

- **Type:** mapping
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml, vars: { mode: lab } }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `external`
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `provision[].host_vars`

Variables per machine (a machine's name -> its variables), on its line of the inventory Isoloom writes: what a playbook keys on per host (its domain, a role flag).

- **Type:** map of name to mapping
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml, host_vars: { a: { mode: lab } } }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp), `external`
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `provision[].requirements`

The Ansible Galaxy requirements to install first (collections, roles); by default `requirements.yml` next to the playbook, when there is one.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `provision: [{ ansible: site.yml, requirements: requirements.yml }]`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp)
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`, `external`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

## `controller`

### `controller`

The controller Isoloom adds for `provision:` (and checks run from it): a small VM, sized and boxed like a machine. By default 1 CPU, 512 MB and a minimal Alpine box on Vagrant.

- **Type:** mapping
- **Example:** `controller: { resources: { cpus: 1 } }`
- **Rendered by:** `vagrant`, `proxmox`, `esxi`
- **Partly rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (aws), `cloud-vm` (azure), `cloud-vm` (gcp) (not yet: `cpus` and `disk_gb`)
- **Refused by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `docker-vm`, `cloud-docker`: environment-level provisioning (`provision:`) runs on VM targets for now
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (digitalocean): DigitalOcean cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (linode): Linode cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Refused by:** `cloud-vm` (oci): Oracle Cloud cloud-vm has no Ansible controller yet
- **Planned for:** `hybrid`
- **Not used by:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `controller.image`

The box to use instead of Isoloom's (Vagrant): a specific Ansible version, a mirror.

- **Type:** mapping
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.vagrant`

A Vagrant box name (e.g. `StefanScherer/windows_2019`).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.vagrant_version`

The box version to pin.

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.qemu`

The box Vagrant's QEMU provider boots instead (libvirt format), when `vagrant` has none (e.g. `peru/windows-server-2019-standard-x64-eval`).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.hyperv`

The box Vagrant's Hyper-V provider boots instead, when `vagrant` has no Hyper-V build (its latest version that has one).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.winrm`

How this Windows box answers WinRM, when it isn't the usual plain-HTTP box.

- **Type:** string
- **Allowed:**
  - `plaintext`: HTTP on 5985, basic auth (the default for the common Windows boxes).
  - `ssl`: HTTPS on 5986, NTLM (certificate not verified).
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.winssh`

This Windows box answers OpenSSH (Windows' own `sshd`, PowerShell as its shell) instead of WinRM: Vagrant connects with `config.winssh` and the playbooks over SSH, as the box's `vagrant` account. Not with `winrm`.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.box_url`

Where Vagrant downloads the `vagrant` box from, when it isn't on Vagrant Cloud: a URL, or a `.box` file in the project (list its folder in `.isoloomignore`, or the project copied into every VM carries it).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.box_server_url`

The box server Vagrant looks the `vagrant` box up on, instead of Vagrant Cloud (a private registry).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.proxmox`

The Proxmox image: a cloud image's URL (the server downloads it), or the id of a template VM on the node (cloned).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.aws`

The AWS image: an AMI id (`ami-0123...`) in the module's region.

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.azure`

The Azure image: a managed image's or gallery image version's resource id.

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.gcp`

The Google Cloud image: `projects/<project>/global/images/<image>` (or `.../family/<f>`).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.digitalocean`

The DigitalOcean image: a slug or a custom image's id.

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.linode`

The Linode image: `linode/<distribution>` or `private/<id>`.

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.image.oci`

The Oracle Cloud image: its OCID (`ocid1.image...`).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.resources`

CPUs, memory (and disk on Proxmox), for many forks against a large environment.

- **Type:** mapping
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.resources.cpus`

CPUs (default 1).

- **Type:** integer
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.resources.memory_mb`

Memory in MB (default 1024).

- **Type:** integer
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.resources.disk_gb`

Disk in GB, for a VM (default 20).

- **Type:** integer
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

### `controller.keep_running`

Keep it running once provisioning is done (to use it as a jump host). By default it halts, keeping its disk: `isoloom test` and `isoloom provision` boot it when they need it.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Default:** `false`
- **Targets:** as [`controller`](#controller)

## `checks`

### `checks`

Black-box checks that prove the behavior on every target: scripts, or declared probes (`http`, `tcp`, `exec`, `script`) run from a machine of the environment. Isoloom adds derived checks of its own from `services` and `reach`.

- **Type:** list of strings or mappings
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`
- **Partly rendered by:** `cloud-vm` (every cloud) (not yet: a check with no `from` and no access machine runs only when a controller exists)
- **Partly rendered by:** `external` (not yet: checks with no machine position; script and playbook checks)

### `checks[].name`

Shown in results. Default: what the check does (`http://web/ from user`).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', expect: 200, wait: 10 }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].from`

The machine the check runs from (its networks, its routes, its view). Default: the access machine when the spec has one, else the environment's networks at once.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', expect: 200, wait: 10 }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `external`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `checks[].http`

An HTTP(S) request to this URL. `expect`: a status code (default 200), `any` (an answer of any status), or `blocked` (nothing answers).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', expect: 200, wait: 10 }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].method`

With `http`: the request method (default GET).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', method: POST }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].headers`

With `http`: request headers.

- **Type:** map of name to string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', headers: { Accept: text/html } }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].body`

With `http`: the request body, sent as is.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', method: POST, body: hello }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].contains`

With `http`: text the response body must contain. With `tcp`: text the bytes read in the first 5 seconds of the connection (after `send`) must contain, like a banner.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', contains: welcome }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].follow`

With `http`: follow redirects (up to 5 hops) and compare the final answer's status, for a page that redirects (a login page, an app's index). Default: the first answer counts. A POST followed by a 301, 302 or 303 goes on as a GET, as in a browser; other methods are sent again to each hop.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', follow: true }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].send`

With `tcp` and `contains`: a line written once connected (followed by a newline; end it with `\r` for CRLF), before reading.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, tcp: 'a:80', send: hello, contains: welcome }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].tcp`

A TCP connection to `host:port`. `expect`: `open` (default) or `blocked`.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, tcp: 'a:80' }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].exec`

A command run inside the `from` machine (`from` is required). `expect`: text its output must contain (default: the command succeeds).

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, exec: 'true' }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `external`
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`

### `checks[].script`

A script in the project, run with sh from the `from` machine's position; it exits 0 when the behavior holds.

- **Type:** string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, script: check.sh }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`
- **Planned for:** `external`

### `checks[].expect`

What counts as passing, in the check's own terms: a status code, `any` or `blocked` for `http`; `open` or `blocked` for `tcp`; text the output contains for `exec`. Each kind's field says its default.

- **Type:** integer or string
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', expect: 200, wait: 10 }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

### `checks[].wait`

Seconds to keep retrying until the check passes: default 30 for `http` and `tcp` (except `blocked`, tried once), 0 for `exec` and `script`.

- **Type:** integer
- **Example:** `checks: [{ name: probe, from: a, http: 'http://a/', expect: 200, wait: 10 }]`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud), `cloud-docker`, `cloud-services`, `external`

## `tools`

### `tools`

Observers beside the environment, on every network, that aren't machines of it (not in `reach`, `resources` or the derived checks): a toolbox to look from (`shell`), or any container image.

- **Type:** map of name to mapping
- **Example:** `tools: { shell: {} }`
- **Rendered by:** `docker`, `hosted`, `vagrant`, `docker-vm`, `hybrid`, `cloud-docker`
- **Planned for:** `kubernetes`, `helm`, `kustomize`, `proxmox`, `esxi`, `cloud-vm` (every cloud)
- **Not used by:** `cloud-services`, `external`

### `tools.*.image`

A container image (needed unless the name is a built-in recipe).

- **Type:** string
- **Targets:** as [`tools`](#tools)

### `tools.*.command`

The command to run, when the image's own isn't right.

- **Type:** list of strings
- **Targets:** as [`tools`](#tools)

### `tools.*.port`

A port the tool serves (its web UI), reachable from every network.

- **Type:** integer
- **Targets:** as [`tools`](#tools)

### `tools.*.publish`

The port on the host's loopback (`127.0.0.1`) that forwards to the tool's `port`, so a browser on the host can open its web UI.

- **Type:** integer
- **Targets:** as [`tools`](#tools)
